notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); no hardware was attached and no hardware or sim backend run is claimed. ENTRY: the card's entry symbol multiagent_mujoco.mujoco_multi:MujocoMulti was found at multiagent_mujoco/mujoco_multi.py:29; the card's family-config decision and MujocoDriver helper were kept, so there is no DEVIATION FROM THE CARD. WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], multiagent_mujoco/assets/coupled_half_cheetah.xml, as a simulated R0 world.sim. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [12 numbers]}}; the bridge checks each ctrl element against the model's per-actuator actuator_ctrlrange before writing data.ctrl. The serviced model's twelve motors inherit the default ctrlrange -1 to 1 (coupled_half_cheetah.xml:36 and :126-138) and the option timestep is 0.01 s (:39). cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward; the state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed). The model is read from the read-only clone in place and is never copied into the package or imported. The class attribute native names the card's entry symbol for provenance; a MujocoDriver's backend object is the injectable mujoco module (families.py), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module. NOT COVERED: the multi-agent layer of MujocoMulti (scenario and agent_conf partitions, per-agent observations, reward, episode limit and the TimeLimit wrapper) is not served; the upstream CoupledHalfCheetah wraps this model in mujoco-py with frame_skip 5 and resets with noise, while the bridge advances one physics tick per tick and resets to mj_resetData defaults; only the card's models[0] is served, the manyagent_ant and manyagent_swimmer assets and the auto-generated manyagent models are not; no viewer, rendering or camera stream is exposed. MuJoCo and mujoco-py were not importable where the gate ran (no network, no pip), so fake.py parses the same MJCF for the joint layout (18 qpos/qvel entries), the twelve actuators and their control ranges, but integrates a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control value; it loads no mesh, resolves no contact, friction, damping, gear, tendon or actuator constraint (the model's spatial tendon coupling t1 and t2 is ignored), and no trajectory was compared with the real engine or the upstream scenario. The real sim path (a backend name backends does not list, which imports the real mujoco module and loads the same file) was not run. WARNINGS (none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake is a stand-in for the mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder (this is the MuJoCo family shape; it is not the upstream simulator and was not compared with it), and G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived seed, ticks and action.ctrl inputs, which PLAYBOOK.md section 8 calls expected for Gymnasium and MuJoCo drivers. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. There are no operator-required limits, so no site-limits.example.json is needed. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds six cases (model shape from the card model, per-actuator control-range refusals with zero effect, state following the control value, reset to the model defaults, the published fidelity contract and the e-stop latch); they pass in G9. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
